title: A failed rehearsal with Guy Kelly and a lost Victor date
summary: He describes a fight between two trumpet players that ended one planned Victor date, and a second that failed because the trombonist could not learn the numbers.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong

blocks.x: I tried to get up a group of very fine Negro players, but I made the mistake...
Was it Guy Kelly or somebody?

I'm sure one of them was Guy Kelly and the other one, I can't remember his name. Guy Kelly was a tough, hard to get along with Negro and the other fellow was an easygoing fellow. Both of them were top-notch cornet players, trumpet players.
Would it have been Chris Kelly by any chance? Do you remember? It was Guy Kelly. Was it Chris Kelly of Blue? Oh, I really,
I can't remember the names. I'm not sure. I know this, that they both played in Celestine's band at the same time. I don't know,
I don't know what Celestine was doing. It was Schatz for a while. It was Schatz Madison.

I don't know, but one of them was a mean man and the other one was, one trumpet player was a mean guy and the other one was a very nice fellow. Well, I set them to rehearsing across, Wailines had a sort of a warehouse across the street and without getting any permission because I knew I couldn't get permission for this, I just took it upon myself to take them over there. The Victor recording people were coming down pretty soon and I was trying to rehearse them for a date with the Victor people. and I just took them over there and they got in a fuss with each other, fight with each other and caused such a commotion that the wrap trunk people who were down below them rang up Wailines and wanted to know what all that commotion was. So Wailines rang down to the band incident department and I don't know how I got the information but I got it, I got it quick enough to go over there and get that band out of there before I got myself in trouble and that was the end of an awful good record date because there were two top notch trumpet players and a fine clarinet player and trombone and piano. I don't think I had the whole band together because it's easy enough to put in a bass and a drum, you know, but that was the end of that recording date. Oh and we had a, we had a date lined up which could have been very good. I'll tell you about this date but I won't mention the name of the trombone player who got to be very famous. Snoozer Quinn, I was going to use, it was another Victor date. I was going to use Snoozer Quinn on guitar and Siegfried Christensen on piano and Eddie Miller on clarinet and I was going to play cornet and there was a trombone player who was playing around town then. Well, we rehearsed that were going to be original numbers. Well, we rehearsed and the trombone player couldn't learn it the first day. So we rehearsed another time and he couldn't learn it the next day. He couldn't, he just couldn't learn the thing. So that was the end of that. I just gave up in disappointment. But what a pity to have lost that. And at that time
